transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The 4C code on Samsung washing machines means the machine is not filling with water fast enough within the first few minutes of starting a cycle. This is almost always caused by a restriction in the water supply rather than a major fault. 1. Ensure the tap behind the machine is turned fully on and the hose isn't kinked or squashed against the wall.
2. Turn off the tap, unscrew the fill hose from the back of the machine, and check the small mesh filter inside the inlet port. If it's blocked with grit or scale, clean it under a tap and reattach.
Tap was open, I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway, no change. Hose isn't kinked. I'll unscrew the hose at the machine end and check the filter now.

That sounds like a good plan. The 4C code is almost always caused by restricted water flow into the machine. If the mesh filter inside the inlet port was blocked with grit or limescale, cleaning it should resolve the issue immediately. However, if the filter was already clean, we need to check if your household water pressure is sufficient. Please let me know what you find with the filter and whether the tap flow seems strong when disconnected.
Filter's clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. Cleaning it now and will refit and retry.

That sounds like exactly what was causing it. The 4C code is triggered when the water flow into the drum isn't fast enough, and a filter clogged with grit or limescale is the most common culprit. Please refit the hose securely, turn the tap back on fully, and start a cycle to see if the error clears. If it still shows 4C after cleaning, we'll need to check your household water pressure next.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Refitted the hose, tap fully on, and started a cycle. It's filling normally now and the 4C has gone.

That is excellent news. To help prevent this from happening again, I recommend checking that inlet filter every few months or if you notice the filling time getting longer. If you have any other questions about your Samsung washing machine, just let me know.
